prize_parts.citation: For developing targeted protein degradation by induced proximity to an E3 ubiquitin ligase, through bifunctional PROTAC degraders and the identification of cereblon as the target of thalidomide-class molecular glues.

statement.case_for: After the first round my preferred configuration is unchanged: one part, B036, credited to Crews, Deshaies and Handa. The chair's summary confirms that the mechanism is not in dispute. Every member who discussed it accepts E3-directed degradation, cereblon as the thalidomide target and the structurally confirmed ternary complexes, and all eight members either prefer B036 or list it as an alternative. What remains open is scope and attribution, which is what a citation can settle. I would word it around the principle, induced proximity to an E3 ligase, with PROTACs as the designed form and cereblon-dependent glues as the discovered form. Each of the three names then carries a distinct, independently reproduced element: the heterobifunctional concept (Crews, Deshaies) and the molecular identity of the glue target (Handa). Degradation is also quantitatively measurable, through degradation kinetics, ternary-complex cooperativity and the hook effect, which is the standard of evidence I apply to everything.
statement.case_against: Two real weaknesses remain. First, the three-name limit excludes Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito, and the PROTAC half rests on two people while the glue half rests on one, so the citation is somewhat lopsided. Second, no degrader drug is approved as far as I know, so the practical payoff is still arriving. I do not think approval is the test, since the mechanism has been reproduced in many laboratories, but a committee that wants clinical proof would reasonably wait. I also accept that a single induced-proximity citation merges two discoveries made at different times by different groups, and the expert report must show that the principle is unified and not just a label.

responses.point: Linke argues that B014 has a cleaner attribution than B036, because the 2009 founding observation and Rosen's quantitative framework are separable, while five top-three rankings for B036 show popularity and not settled credit.
responses.response: I agree that support counts do not settle attribution, and I am not relying on them. But a clean attribution is not a stronger scientific case. For B014 the chair's own summary lists contested points: whether in vivo condensates are equilibrium liquid phases, whether the Hyman and Brangwynne observation is chemistry or cell biology, and whether Pappu and Mittag should be credited. Those are scientific questions about what was established, and several early in-cell claims changed when measured quantitatively. For B036 the open questions concern who is the third name and how wide the citation is, while the mechanism and the credit for the originating discoveries are not in doubt. If the principle-only citation Linke and Sparr describe could be written without claiming that cellular condensates are liquids, B014 would move up for me, which is why it stays my first alternative, but it has not overtaken B036.

responses.point: Zou would accept Ciulli replacing Handa if the prize is framed around the PROTAC design principle, and notes that a Handa-based citation is lopsided because the glue half rests on one mechanistic discovery.
responses.response: I accept the lopsidedness and I will not claim that three names balance two lines. Where I differ is on what the citation is about. Without Handa the thalidomide-class glues, the part of the field that was found and not designed, lose their molecular anchor, and the principle becomes a statement about engineered bifunctional molecules only. Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures made PROTACs drug-like and explain selectivity, which I value, but they refine a concept Crews and Deshaies had already shown in cells. I would take Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli over no prize, but with the induced-proximity wording that the chair's question points to, Handa is the better third name.

responses.point: Aqvist says the prize would honour a mechanism and modality with the clinical payoff still developing, that the citation should name the principle and not the pipeline, and that B023 is the better-matured choice if the committee finds B036 early.
responses.response: I agree with the first two points and have changed the wording of my citation in response: it now names induced proximity to an E3 ligase and mentions no clinical outcome. On B023 I asked him in round one whether the funnel picture made predictions that experiments later confirmed, and the chair's summary shows the questions about the 2024 protein structure prize and the Wolynes, Onuchic, Fersht, Dill and Bryngelson attribution are still open. That keeps it behind B036 for me. His own statement that he would not fight a B023 outcome, but also that he moved B036 above it, suggests that B036 is the position he accepts as stronger on balance, and I take that as agreement and not as a counter-argument.

responses.point: Brzezinski proposes a two-part prize, B067 (Gray and Winkler, protein electron transfer) with B066 (Shokat, covalent KRAS), and notes that the two topics are fairly unrelated and lack the breadth of B036.
responses.response: B067 is rigorous, and the experimental attribution to Gray and Winkler is clean, but the question he raises himself is the right one: whether protein kinetics is a distinct achievement after the 1992 electron-transfer prize and the tunnelling-pathway theory that sits outside the credited pair. I cannot judge that as well as he can, and it is a reason for caution. For B066 I find the chemistry convincing, but it is one covalent chemistry on one target, with clinical durability still under study, and it would be a narrower choice than an induced-proximity principle that applies to many targets. A two-part prize needs five votes behind both parts, and I do not see a majority for this pairing on the evidence in the first round.

responses.point: Aili backs the Crews, Deshaies and Handa trio and asks whether the prize should centre on PROTACs or on molecular glues, noting that any trio risks reading as a judgment about which line ranks first.
responses.response: My view is that the citation should centre on neither but on the shared principle, and that the three names are not ranked: Crews and Deshaies for the designed bifunctional degrader, Handa for the mechanism that explains the glues. I think the risk Aili names is real but small if the wording says plainly that the prize is for the principle and that later contributors (Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim, Ito) extended it. I did not move toward a PROTAC-only or glue-only citation, because splitting them would lead to the two-part configuration, which would need the same three-person limit to cover more ground and weaken the case for each.

uncertainties: Whether Handa or Ciulli is the better third name; this is the one point where I could be persuaded, if the expert report shows that the VHL-ligand and ternary-complex work defines the principle and not just its refinement.
Whether a majority accepts that clinical approval is not needed; I cannot verify the current regulatory status of any degrader.
Whether the original PROTAC credit between Crews, Deshaies and Sakamoto is fully settled; I am recalling this and have not checked the primary papers.
Whether a principle-only B014 citation can be written that leaves the in vivo condensate debate out of the claim.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal to disclose, unchanged from round 1. I have no institutional, collaborative or financial link to Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli or any other credited name on the shortlist, and my work on nucleotide metabolism at Umeå is not directly related to ubiquitin-dependent degradation. I did note that the chair's summary shows no recusal flag involving me.
